doc.title: Michael Moore interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 12, 1997

title: Hearing himself on Rebecca Kilgore's 'I Saw Stars'
summary: Monk plays a track from the Kilgore CD and Moore reacts to hearing himself and the recorded sound.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: I wanted to play something for you, and see if you recognize this.
Now, this will give it away.
Oh, that’s Becky Kilgore. Yeah, I recognized me, in fact, is that on the record?
Yeah. It’s called, that’s the remake of “The Duke.” Tough tune.
I was just looking at it and I said well let me see how he felt about playing on this tune.
That’s nice. I don’t think I ever heard it.
No kidding? You do so much recording that you probably don’t always get to really—
Well I have this record, and I remember, this is the one, “I Saw Stars,” right?

I wonder if I got a cassette of that or something. See, maybe it’s not on a cassette. But I didn’t think it was on the one I had. Because you know Dan Barrett said you know, “I love your solo” on something, and I said, “Really?”
Well it’s there. You think you’ll have to go out and buy it?

They got it here. No I do have that, and I love the way Rebecca sounds on there, I just think it’s great. Well thank you for playing that. It’s always nice to hear myself play something that I like. And it was nicely recorded. A lot of times, a big problem with the bass is the recorded sound. A lot of times it’s tough.
They just don’t know how you think?
